points.text: 1 mp1 = resistance with ref. to P / Q / R Y, is resistant to Q / has no resistance to P ;
points.guidance: A Y has some resistance to (antibiotic) R

points.text: 2 mp2 = antibiotics used at different concentrations (antibiotic) R may, have different concentration / be less effective, compared with P ;
3 mp3 = reason for resistance ref. to gene(s) for resistance (on plasmids) or Y has, cell wall / cell membrane, that prevents entry of antibiotic Q or Y has enzyme that breaks down, Q / R ;
4 mp4 = action of antibiotics idea that antibiotics have, different / specific, target(s) / AW ;
points.guidance: A any example of process inhibited by antibiotic, e.g. cell wall synthesis transcription translation DNA replication cell surface membrane function synthesis of folic acid

points.text: 5 mp5 = AVP ; e.g. idea that P may be bacteriocidal / (antibiotic) R is bacteriostatic e.g. idea that gene for resistance to antibiotic R passed by, vertical / horizontal, transmission

points.guidance: to award the MP1 to MP5 you must be able to see a difference between the two stated clearly

points.text: 1 vaccines (generally) are preventative / are not a treatment / are not a cure or use before a person, has an infection / is ill v antibiotics are (generally) not preventative / are a treatment / are a cure or used when a person, has an infection / is ill ;
2 vaccines effective against bacteria and viruses (in context of different vaccines) v antibiotics not effective against viruses / only effect against bacteria ;
3 vaccines idea of indirect effect on pathogens v antibiotics idea of direct effect on pathogens ;
4 vaccines not given as a course / give once or a few times (or with boosters) v antibiotics given as a course / over many days / AW ;
5 vaccines specific for particular, pathogen v (most) antibiotics act on a range of pathogens ;
6 vaccines stimulate an immune response or antibiotics do not stimulate an immune response ;
7 vaccines detail e.g. stimulate, (B- / T-) lymphocytes / production of antibodies or antibiotics do not stimulate, (B- / T-) lymphocytes / production of antibodies ;
points.guidance: A stimulates production of memory cells / A no stimulation of memory cells

points.text: 8 vaccines provide long-term, protection / immunity or antibiotics do not provide long-term, protection / immunity ;
9 vaccines does not lead to resistance or antibiotics may lead to resistance ;
10 vaccines time delay before being effective / AW or antibiotics have effect, faster / sooner / AW ;
